clue.text: Keen to add to score, perhaps

definitions.meaning: keen as in having a fine cutting edge
in music a sign added to a written score raises a note by a semitone

explanation.surface: Someone eager to put more points on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen blade is a cutting one, and in musical notation the sign raising a note a semitone is written onto the score.

clue.text: Adherent left in jolly good surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the word for jolly good encloses the word for left

parts.note: super is a British exclamation of approval
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A loyal follower kept in good spirits by those around.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter is a follower or backer of a cause or team.

clue.text: Guided missile school hasn't opened

indicators.note: not opened means the school's name lacks its first letter

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school that has not started its weapons programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't opened' drops the first letter, H, from HARROW, the London public school.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a projectile aimed and shot from a bow.

clue.text: Guy perhaps for Beatrix about fifty

indicators.note: about means the author's surname goes round the numeral

parts.note: Beatrix Potter wrote the Peter Rabbit books
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A chap who is fond of Beatrix at about fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes plotted the 1605 Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament. 'about' puts L inside POTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Fawkes was a conspirator in the scheme to blow up Parliament, an example of a schemer.

clue.text: Bangers served daily?

parts.note: a report is the bang of a gun, so those who make reports are bangers, and journalists on a daily paper turn them out every day

explanation.surface: Sausages dished up every morning at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangers are British sausages, so the surface is about breakfast; the cryptic reading takes a report as a loud bang, and journalists produce reports daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists file reports, and a report is also the bang of a gun, so a newspaper's staff are playfully its bangers.

clue.text: Troublesome IRA lot in Venice?

indicators.note: troublesome means the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A troublemaking terrorist group on the loose in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troublesome' rearranges IRA and LOT; the definition is a place in Venice, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous bridge and business district on the Grand Canal in Venice.

clue.text: Claim money round about end, of August

indicators.note: round means the money word goes around the other letters

parts.note: pence are British coins
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: end means the final letter of August is taken

explanation.surface: Demanding cash around the close of the summer month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts RE and T, the last letter of August picked by 'end', inside PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a claim, often a false one, as in making a pretence to learning.

clue.text: Double crop for Cheshire town

parts.note: to double is to run, as in moving at the double
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A bumper harvest for a town in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Runcorn is an industrial town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Runcorn is a town on the Mersey estuary in that English county.

clue.text: Strange device for a mountaineer

parts.note: quotes Longfellow's poem in which a youth climbing an Alpine pass carries a banner bearing a strange device, a Latin motto

explanation.surface: An odd gadget for a climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'device' looks like a gadget; it is the motto on a banner in Longfellow's poem about a doomed climber.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto meaning ever higher, written on the banner in Longfellow's poem of that name.

clue.text: Describes raspberry jam? Not very well

definitions.meaning: raspberry jam is full of little pips

explanation.surface: A judgement of a jar of preserves and of someone feeling poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Raspberry jam is full of pips, and someone off-colour feels shabby and unwell.

clue.text: Filter supplied by firm with some delay

parts.note: per means by way of or by means of
CO is short for company, a firm
late means arriving after the expected time

explanation.surface: A water filter delivered by a company, behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To percolate is to seep slowly through something, the way coffee passes through a filter.

clue.text: Name smallholding yielding shellfish

parts.note: an acre is a small plot of land

explanation.surface: A named little farm that produces shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: nacre, mother-of-pearl, is what shellfish yield, and 'yielding' joins the wordplay to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl, the lustrous lining of oyster and mussel shells, is produced by those molluscs.

clue.text: Operatic aria in hotel — Tom Whitney arranged it

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the three words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A singer called Tom Whitney performs an opera number at a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles the fifteen letters of HOTEL, TOM and WHITNEY; 'it' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The English title of 'Vesti la giubba', the famous tenor aria from Leoncavallo's opera Pagliacci.

clue.text: Possible explanation of little boy going by railway

parts.note: Theo is a short form of the boy's name Theodore

explanation.surface: Accounting for a small child travelling by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed account of why something happens, not yet proven.

clue.text: Leaving out former church training upset no-one

parts.note: ex means former
CE is the Church of England
PT is physical training

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Quitting an old church because nobody was upset by the training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses NO and I to give ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An exception is something left out of a general rule.

clue.text: Examines one on metrical analysis

parts.note: to scan is to look over closely
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone studies a poem's rhythm by scrutinising it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scansion is the working out of a verse's rhythm, marking stressed and unstressed syllables.

clue.text: The opposite of seaside spring flowers

definitions.text: The opposite of seaside spring flowers

parts.words: The opposite of seaside spring flowers
parts.note: flowers are things that flow, and the highest flows at the coast are spring tides, whose counterpart is the lowest range

explanation.surface: The reverse of blooms growing by the sea in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' looks like blooms; read it as things that flow. Spring tides have the greatest range, and their counterpart has the least.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides of least range, at the moon's first and third quarters, contrast with the biggest tides.

clue.text: Show skeleton

parts.note: the bare outline of a play or film, its plot skeleton

explanation.surface: Displaying a set of bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a verb, display; it is a noun, a stage show or film whose outline is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a plot outline of a play or film.

clue.text: Wrinkle connected with wine bag

parts.note: a ruck is a crease or fold in cloth
sack is an old name for a dry white wine from Spain

explanation.surface: A crumpled carrier tied up with a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK is an old Spanish or Canary wine, familiar from Falstaff in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is a backpack, a bag carried on the shoulders.

clue.text: A number in view having unequal sides

indicators.note: in places the letters within the view word

parts.note: a scene is a view
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a number

explanation.surface: A number of points visible with lopsided edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalene triangle has three sides of different lengths.

clue.text: Peninsula has variety of Brie — excellent when retiring

indicators.note: a variety of the cheese means its letters come in another form
retiring means drawing back, so the word for excellent is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A region that boasts a fine type of cheese, best enjoyed at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges BRIE to IBER; 'when retiring' turns AI round to IA. The printed count says 7 but the answer has six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian peninsula is the south-western tip of Europe holding Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Pet animals?

parts.note: the household pet's name splits into two other beasts, a male cow and a hound

explanation.surface: Animals kept at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The pet's breed name is two animals in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulldog is a breed of dog kept as a pet, its name made of two creatures.

clue.text: Money for a horse

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: Cash paid out for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a sum, especially of money.

clue.text: Master author of Stevenson's character

parts.note: a ship's master is its captain
Tobias Smollett was an eighteenth-century Scottish novelist

explanation.surface: A great writer creating one of Robert Louis Stevenson's figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The honest commander of the Hispaniola in Robert Louis Stevenson's novel Treasure Island.

clue.text: Embrace in which Bobby holds Sal when upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the whole is turned upside down, read backwards
holds means the policeman's letters enclose the name

parts.note: PC is police constable, a bobby being a British policeman

explanation.surface: A policeman hugs a distressed woman called Sal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts SAL inside PC to give PSALC; 'when upset' turns it all round. A bobby is a British police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp someone is to hold them tightly, to hug.

clue.text: Escape from the Geneva Declaration

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Getting away from an international agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across GenEVA DEclaration.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or avoid.

clue.text: A point about wood for burning

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first two pieces wrap the tree

parts.note: E is a compass point, east
fir is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: A tip about which logs make good fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afire is on fire, ablaze.

clue.text: Used by clerk writing circular letters?

definitions.text: Used by clerk writing circular letters?

parts.words: Used by clerk writing circular letters?
parts.note: a clerk's style of penmanship with rounded letters is taken as one writing circulars

explanation.surface: An office worker sending out a mailshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular letters' looks like a mass mailing; it means letters shaped round, a clerk's traditional script.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear, rounded style of handwriting once taught to clerks for ledgers and documents.

clue.text: Write to leader in some cricket festival

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: in places the leader's letters within the cricket match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
CO, commanding officer, is a military leader

explanation.surface: Sending a letter to a team captain during a cricket celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only links. A Test match is a top-level international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitsun, the Christian feast seven weeks after Easter, is a church festival.

clue.text: Think of Americans

parts.note: an American saying they suppose something uses a word meaning conjecture

explanation.surface: Consider the people of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Americans' marks the US idiom 'I suppose' meaning 'I think'.
explanation.definitionFit: In American speech 'I guess so' is the everyday way to say 'I believe so'.
